assessments.reasoning: The statistikportal.frankfurt.de origin, city copyright footer and German licence section establish municipal publication. The whole-page SHA-256 matches c109b5ea9901c7d1a4b6b08e7035d3303d70e143c634f38a66eeee3a1ca55655.

The Index’s own Scope and identities document at cdff8aeed68bf1f9c62d8c86159c7dc08b2d75d7 includes relevant data terms and defines the License criterion. The municipal text supplies the grant and edition needed to apply that criterion.

The FITKO-hosted GovData documentation independently identifies the BY edition and links its full name to the same GovData route. It labels its extracts as copied from the original. This supports the link and edition context without supplying an independent legal text.

challenge.method: Compared the complete municipal licence section, its heading, link and footer with GovData’s documentation, including its conditions and alternatives table. Tested attribution versus Zero, municipal publication versus national authorship, and whether the municipal text is a verbatim transcription.
challenge.results: Both sources name attribution 2.0 and link to https://www.govdata.de/dl-de/by-2-0. Both identify the provider, licence reference, dataset reference and change notice. GovData lists Zero as a more permissive alternative. Frankfurt combines the licence and dataset references in one bullet and repeats a business-process sentence inside its attribution list. Its unusual “DL-DE->BY-2.0” heading does not outweigh the full name, operative clauses and link. These differences defeat a verbatim-copy inference while preserving the scoped identity.

limitations: Frankfurt qualifies its applicability statement with “Soweit bei den Daten nichts Anderes vermerkt ist.” The evidence supports publication of this municipal copy. A particular dataset’s governing terms, redistribution rights and installation eligibility require separate evidence.
Active is the intended Index lifecycle value. Current admission would require a qualified selection and the corresponding registry bindings.

Under the task brief and SCES §9, release qualification requires separate gates A–E.
reasoning: Frankfurt’s official municipal election site publishes a German text expressly named Datenlizenz Deutschland – Namensnennung – Version 2.0. The captured HTML matches the claim’s representation digest. Its three numbered clauses grant use of data and metadata, specify attribution and require changes to be marked. This meets the Index criterion of an identifiable grant with a text and edition. SCES §§1–4 require authority for the precise proposition and a challenge to identity merges. Frankfurt has direct authority for what it publishes on its site. GovData’s own documentation separately confirms the edition name and destination.
